proj_kitchen_about_body: A modern farmhouse kitchen built around a large island for entertaining. Quartz counters with a waterfall edge, a farmhouse sink, and custom-built open shelving.
proj_kitchen_qa_1_q: What was the client's vision for this kitchen?
proj_kitchen_qa_1_a: The client wanted a modern farmhouse-style kitchen with a large island for entertaining.
proj_kitchen_qa_2_q: What are some of the standout features of the new kitchen?
proj_kitchen_qa_2_a: The standout features include a beautiful quartz countertop with a waterfall edge, a farmhouse sink, and custom-built open shelving.
proj_kitchen_qa_3_q: How did you address the lighting in the new kitchen?
proj_kitchen_qa_3_a: We installed a combination of recessed lighting, under-cabinet lighting, and two large pendant lights over the island to create a bright and inviting space.
proj_bathroom_about_body: A full primary-bath remodel: walk-in shower with frameless glass, floating double vanity, and heated tile floors. Waterproofed to code and finished with matte-black fixtures.
proj_bathroom_qa_1_q: What did the client want to change about the old bathroom?
proj_bathroom_qa_1_a: They were tired of a cramped tub-shower combo and wanted a proper walk-in shower with better storage on the vanity.
proj_bathroom_qa_2_a: We used a full liquid membrane behind the tile, sealed all penetrations, and pitched the shower pan to a linear drain — no shortcuts.
proj_bathroom_qa_3_a: For a primary bath in a cold-tile install, yes. It's a modest add on the electrical side and the client uses it eight months of the year.
proj_wood_about_body: A floor-to-ceiling white-oak slat wall behind the living-room sofa. Milled on site so the reveals line up, then finished with a low-sheen hardwax oil.
proj_wood_qa_1_q: Why white oak and not a cheaper species?
proj_wood_qa_1_a: White oak takes a natural finish beautifully and stays dimensionally stable in a climate-controlled room. Softer woods would telegraph seasonal movement.
proj_wood_qa_2_a: A plywood backer painted charcoal, then each slat glued and pin-nailed. The pin holes disappear into the grain after finishing.
proj_wood_qa_3_q: Can you do the same in a room with a TV?
proj_wood_qa_3_a: Yes — we flush-mount the TV bracket to a blocked section and route the cabling behind the slats before install.
proj_lighting_about_body: Low-voltage path, uplight and downlight package around the front elevation and back patio. Warm 2700K throughout, on an astronomical timer so it tracks sunset year-round.
proj_lighting_qa_1_q: Why low voltage instead of line voltage?
proj_lighting_qa_1_a: It's safer around beds and irrigation, easier to reposition as plantings grow, and the fixtures last longer at 12V.
proj_lighting_qa_2_q: How many fixtures did you use?
proj_lighting_qa_2_a: Twenty-two: six uplights on the trees, eight path lights along the walk, four downlights in the eaves, and four wash lights on the back patio.
proj_lighting_qa_3_a: Very little. Wipe the lenses once a year, and check for anything a mower or edger may have shifted. LEDs at this wattage should run for a decade.
proj_cabinet_about_body: A shaker-style cabinet install in a kitchen we didn't design but wanted to make right. Boxes leveled, doors aligned, and soft-close hardware fitted throughout.
proj_cabinet_qa_1_q: Do you install cabinets you didn't supply?
proj_cabinet_qa_1_a: Yes — we're happy to install cabinets the client bought elsewhere. We inspect the shipment first and flag anything damaged before we start.
proj_cabinet_qa_2_q: What does a proper install involve?
proj_cabinet_qa_2_a: Leveling the boxes to the highest point on the floor, shimming to the wall, screwing into studs, and adjusting every door and drawer front for even reveals.
proj_cabinet_qa_3_a: We drill for hardware using a template so pulls and knobs line up perfectly. If the client changes hardware later, the template travels with the kitchen.
proj_tile_about_body: A covered back patio finished in large-format porcelain tile rated for exterior use. Set on a mud bed with the fall pitched away from the house, grouted with a flexible epoxy.
proj_tile_qa_1_a: Porcelain is dense, doesn't absorb water, and holds up to freeze-thaw. Natural stone works too but needs sealing on a schedule.
proj_tile_qa_2_q: Does the tile get slippery when wet?
proj_tile_qa_2_a: We spec a matte, structured finish rated R11 for exterior wet areas. It has grip underfoot without feeling rough.
proj_tile_qa_3_q: How do you keep water off the house?
proj_tile_qa_3_a: The slab is pitched a quarter-inch per foot away from the wall and the tile follows that pitch. Water runs to the edge, not the door threshold.
